steps.title: 고장 났어요
steps.goal: 기계 문제를 설명하고 해결 방법을 묻고 권하기
steps.scene_desc: 1월 초 아침, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 지우가 노트북의 까만 화면을 가리키며 휴대폰을 귀에 대고 통화하고, 맞은편의 대니얼이 커피잔을 든 채 고개를 끄덕임. 창밖은 겨울 거리(화면·간판에 글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "My laptop keeps freezing." (고장 났어요). Goal: 기계 문제를 설명하고 해결 방법을 묻고 권하기. Today's scene: 1월 초 아침, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 지우가 노트북의 까만 화면을 가리키며 휴대폰을 귀에 대고 통화하고, 맞은편의 대니얼이 커피잔을 든 채 고개를 끄덕임. 창밖은 겨울 거리(화면·간판에 글자 없이). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "My ___ keeps ___ing.".

steps.when: 같은 문제가 자꾸 되풀이될 때 써요. keep 뒤에는 *-ing*.
steps.extra: My laptop keeps freezing. · My phone keeps crashing.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "My ___ keeps ___ing." (내 ~가 자꾸 ~해요.). When to use it: 같은 문제가 자꾸 되풀이될 때 써요. keep 뒤에는 -ing. Note: My laptop keeps freezing. · My phone keeps crashing.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "It stopped working.".

steps.when: 잘 되던 기계가 멈췄을 때 써요. stop 뒤에도 *-ing*.
steps.extra: My mouse stopped working. · It won’t turn on.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "It stopped working." (작동을 멈췄어요. 고장 났어요.). When to use it: 잘 되던 기계가 멈췄을 때 써요. stop 뒤에도 -ing. Note: My mouse stopped working. · It won’t turn on.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Have you tried turning it off and on again?".

steps.en: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
steps.when: 간단한 해결 방법을 권해요. Have you tried + *-ing*? = ~해 봤어요?
steps.extra: 대답: Yes, multiple times. · Not yet. I’ll try.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Have you tried turning it off and on again?" (껐다가 다시 켜 봤어요?). When to use it: 간단한 해결 방법을 권해요. Have you tried + -ing? = ~해 봤어요? Note: 대답: Yes, multiple times. · Not yet. I’ll try.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Frozen Again · 1월 초 아침, 동네 카페에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: Frozen Again · 1월 초 아침, 동네 카페에서

lines.en: Morning, Jiwoo! You look stressed. What’s wrong?
lines.ko: 좋은 아침이에요, 지우 씨! 스트레스받은 얼굴이네요. 무슨 일이에요?

lines.en: {{My laptop keeps freezing.}} And I have to send a big design file today!
lines.ko: 노트북이 자꾸 멈춰요. 오늘 큰 디자인 파일을 보내야 하는데!

lines.en: Oh no. {{Have you tried turning it off and on again?}}
lines.ko: 저런. 껐다가 다시 켜 봤어요?

lines.en: Yes, multiple times. It works for a few minutes, and then it freezes again. Oh no… now the screen just went black. {{It stopped working}}!
lines.ko: 네, 여러 번요. 몇 분 되다가 또 멈춰요. 아, 이런… 이번엔 화면이 그냥 까매졌어요. 아예 멈췄어요!

lines.en: Hmm. It doesn’t look like a virus. Did you install anything new? And is it still under warranty?
lines.ko: 음. 바이러스 같지는 않네요. 새로 설치한 거 있어요? 그리고 아직 보증 기간이에요?

lines.en: Just an update last night. And yes, I think it’s still under warranty. I’ll call the repair center.
lines.ko: 어젯밤에 업데이트 하나만요. 그리고 네, 아직 보증 기간인 것 같아요. 수리 센터에 전화해 볼게요.

lines.en: Repair center. I’m a technician. How can I help you?
lines.ko: 수리 센터입니다. 저는 수리 기사예요. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?

lines.en: Hi. My laptop keeps freezing, and now it won’t turn on.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 노트북이 자꾸 멈추더니 이제 안 켜져요.

lines.en: Okay. Hold down the power button for ten seconds. Then turn it on again.
lines.ko: 네. 전원 버튼을 10초 동안 꾹 누르세요. 그다음 다시 켜 보세요.

lines.en: Okay… It’s on! It’s working now.
lines.ko: 네… 켜졌어요! 이제 돼요.

lines.en: Good. If it keeps crashing, bring it in. We’ll check the internal parts.
lines.ko: 다행이네요. 계속 꺼지면 가지고 오세요. 내부 부품을 점검해 드릴게요.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Frozen Again · 1월 초 아침, 동네 카페에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Daniel: "Morning, Jiwoo! You look stressed. What’s wrong?" (좋은 아침이에요, 지우 씨! 스트레스받은 얼굴이네요. 무슨 일이에요?)
2. Jiwoo: "My laptop keeps freezing. And I have to send a big design file today!" (노트북이 자꾸 멈춰요. 오늘 큰 디자인 파일을 보내야 하는데!)
3. Daniel: "Oh no. Have you tried turning it off and on again?" (저런. 껐다가 다시 켜 봤어요?)
4. Jiwoo: "Yes, multiple times. It works for a few minutes, and then it freezes again. Oh no… now the screen just went black. It stopped working!" (네, 여러 번요. 몇 분 되다가 또 멈춰요. 아, 이런… 이번엔 화면이 그냥 까매졌어요. 아예 멈췄어요!)
5. Daniel: "Hmm. It doesn’t look like a virus. Did you install anything new? And is it still under warranty?" (음. 바이러스 같지는 않네요. 새로 설치한 거 있어요? 그리고 아직 보증 기간이에요?)
6. Jiwoo: "Just an update last night. And yes, I think it’s still under warranty. I’ll call the repair center." (어젯밤에 업데이트 하나만요. 그리고 네, 아직 보증 기간인 것 같아요. 수리 센터에 전화해 볼게요.)
7. Tech: "Repair center. I’m a technician. How can I help you?" (수리 센터입니다. 저는 수리 기사예요. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?)
8. Jiwoo: "Hi. My laptop keeps freezing, and now it won’t turn on." (안녕하세요. 노트북이 자꾸 멈추더니 이제 안 켜져요.)
9. Tech: "Okay. Hold down the power button for ten seconds. Then turn it on again." (네. 전원 버튼을 10초 동안 꾹 누르세요. 그다음 다시 켜 보세요.)
10. Jiwoo: "Okay… It’s on! It’s working now." (네… 켜졌어요! 이제 돼요.)
11. Tech: "Good. If it keeps crashing, bring it in. We’ll check the internal parts." (다행이네요. 계속 꺼지면 가지고 오세요. 내부 부품을 점검해 드릴게요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Daniel and Tech. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

frame: Have you tried turning it off and on again? / Try plugging it in.
head: 기기
문제 (keep ~ing)
해결 권하기
rows: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
keeps making a noise. 자꾸 소리가 나요
Maybe it needs to be fixed.
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: My ___ keeps ___ing. / It stopped working. / Have you tried turning it off and on again? / Try plugging it in. Table (기기 → 문제 (keep ~ing)):
- My laptop → keeps freezing. 자꾸 멈춰요
- My phone → keeps crashing. 자꾸 꺼져요
- My printer → keeps making a noise. 자꾸 소리가 나요
- My speaker → keeps turning off. 자꾸 꺼져요
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
My laptop *keeps freezing*. 노트북이 자꾸 멈춰요. 
It *keeps making* a strange noise. 자꾸 이상한 소리가 나요. 
It *stopped working*. 작동을 멈췄어요. — 하던 일을 멈추면 stop + -ing
turn on · turn off · it은 가운데

*turn on* the laptop = *turn* the laptop *on* 노트북을 켜다 
it·them은 가운데에만: *turn it off* 그걸 끄다 
Have you tried *turning it off and on again*? try + -ing = 한번 해 보다
errors: The battery runs out so fastly.
The battery runs out so fast.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- keep + -ing · stop + -ing: My laptop keeps freezing. 노트북이 자꾸 멈춰요. / It keeps making a strange noise. 자꾸 이상한 소리가 나요. / It stopped working. 작동을 멈췄어요. — 하던 일을 멈추면 stop + -ing
- turn on · turn off · it은 가운데: turn on the laptop = turn the laptop on 노트북을 켜다 / it·them은 가운데에만: turn it off 그걸 끄다 / Have you tried turning it off and on again? try + -ing = 한번 해 보다
Common mistakes on screen:
- My laptop keeps freeze. → My laptop keeps freezing. (keep 뒤에는 -ing.)
- Did you turn off it? → Did you turn it off? (it은 turn과 off 사이에.)
- It’s not work. → It’s not working. (‘작동하지 않아요’는 be + working.)
- The battery runs out so fastly. → The battery runs out so fast. (fast는 -ly 없이 그대로 ‘빨리’.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: keep + -ing · stop + -ing: My laptop keeps freezing. 노트북이 자꾸 멈춰요. It keeps making a strange noise. 자꾸 이상한 소리가 나요. It stopped working. 작동을 멈췄어요. — 하던 일을 멈추면 stop + -ing
turn on · turn off · it은 가운데: turn on the laptop = turn the laptop on 노트북을 켜다 it·them은 가운데에만: turn it off 그걸 끄다 Have you tried turning it off and on again? try + -ing = 한번 해 보다
mistakes: My laptop keeps freeze. → My laptop keeps freezing.
Did you turn off it? → Did you turn it off?
It’s not work. → It’s not working.
The battery runs out so fastly. → The battery runs out so fast.

steps.note: 예) laptop / freeze → My laptop keeps freezing. — Have you tried turning it off and on again? · 선생님이 해결 방법을 권해요.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) laptop / freeze → My laptop keeps freezing. — Have you tried turning it off and on again? · 선생님이 해결 방법을 권해요. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: laptop → freeze | phone → crash | printer → make a strange noise | speaker → turn off.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

cards: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
steps.teach:
This is the start of session 2 of "My laptop keeps freezing." (고장 났어요); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "My ___ keeps ___ing." / "It stopped working." / "Have you tried turning it off and on again?". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: The battery runs out so fast.
Maybe it needs to be fixed.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 문제 말하기: "The screen just went black." (화면이 그냥 까매졌어요., 보통); "It won’t turn on." (안 켜져요., 보통); "It makes a strange noise." (이상한 소리가 나요., 보통); "The battery runs out so fast." (배터리가 너무 빨리 닳아요., 보통)
- 해결 방법 권하기: "Did you update it?" (업데이트했어요?, 보통); "Try plugging it in." (전원(충전기)을 꽂아 봐요., 보통); "Maybe it needs to be fixed." (고쳐야 할지도 몰라요., 보통)
- 수리 묻기 · 해결됐을 때: "Is it still under warranty?" (아직 보증 기간이에요?, 보통); "It’s working now." (이제 돼요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 기계가 말썽일 때

*freeze* (화면이) 멈추다 · *crash* (갑자기) 꺼지다, 다운되다 
*install* an update 업데이트를 설치하다 · *restore* files 파일을 복구하다 
a *virus* (컴퓨터) 바이러스 · low on *storage* 저장 공간이 부족한 
a search *engine* 검색 엔진 · the mouse *wheel* 마우스 휠
보증·수리 (참고)

Is it still under *warranty*? 아직 보증 기간이에요? 
a *guarantee* 보증, 약속 · the *manufacturer* 제조사 
the technician *in charge* 담당 기사 · *technical* problems 기술적인 문제 
보증 기간·조건은 제품과 구입처마다 달라요. 구입처나 제조사의 최신 안내를 확인하세요. 이 과의 수리 센터는 수업용 가상 장소예요. 
수리 대사는 말하기 연습용이에요. 실제 기기 조작은 제조사 안내를 따르세요. 강제로 끄면 저장하지 않은 작업이 사라질 수 있어요.

A: My laptop keeps ___.   B: Have you tried turning it ___ and on again?

Tips on screen:
- 기계가 말썽일 때: freeze (화면이) 멈추다 · crash (갑자기) 꺼지다, 다운되다 / install an update 업데이트를 설치하다 · restore files 파일을 복구하다 / a virus (컴퓨터) 바이러스 · low on storage 저장 공간이 부족한 / a search engine 검색 엔진 · the mouse wheel 마우스 휠
- 보증·수리 (참고): Is it still under warranty? 아직 보증 기간이에요? / a guarantee 보증, 약속 · the manufacturer 제조사 / the technician in charge 담당 기사 · technical problems 기술적인 문제 / 보증 기간·조건은 제품과 구입처마다 달라요. 구입처나 제조사의 최신 안내를 확인하세요. 이 과의 수리 센터는 수업용 가상 장소예요. / 수리 대사는 말하기 연습용이에요. 실제 기기 조작은 제조사 안내를 따르세요. 강제로 끄면 저장하지 않은 작업이 사라질 수 있어요.

Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: battery (배터리), plug (플러그), cable (케이블, 선), button (버튼), noise (소음, (이상한) 소리), freeze ((화면이) 멈추다), repair (수리; 수리하다), device (기기, 장치), machine (기계), technician (기술자, 수리 기사), component (부품), disk (디스크, 저장 장치).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

items: This machine is easy to operate.

steps.teach:
Word list on screen: crash ((기기·프로그램이) 갑자기 꺼지다) — "My phone keeps crashing."; warranty (품질 보증(기간)) — "Is it still under warranty?"; operate ((기계를) 작동하다, 다루다) — "This machine is easy to operate."; manufacture (제조하다, 만들다) — "It was manufactured last year."; screen (화면) — "The screen just went black."; charge (충전하다) — "Did you charge your phone?"; update (업데이트; 업데이트하다) — "Did you update it?"; fix (고치다) — "Maybe it needs to be fixed."; electronic (전자의) — "electronic devices"; storage (저장 공간) — "My phone is low on storage.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What device do you use the most?" (hint on screen: I use my ___ the most.)
- "Has your phone or laptop ever stopped working? What happened?" (hint on screen: Yes. It kept ___ing. / The screen just went black.)
- "Your friend says, “My laptop keeps freezing.” What do you say?" (hint on screen: Have you tried turning it off and on again?)
- "How often do you update your phone?" (hint on screen: I update it ___. / Only when it asks me to.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.

steps.title: A Small Crack
steps.text: Two days later, Jiwoo’s laptop froze again, so she took it to the repair center. The technician *in charge* opened it up. “There’s a small crack in the fan. It’s part of the internal cooling mechanism,” he said. “And this wire is loose.” Jiwoo asked about her files. “Don’t worry. Your storage disk is fine. We can restore everything.” The repair was free under the manufacturer’s guarantee. He also gave her some tips. “*Turn down* the screen brightness, and back up your files frequently. Electronic devices don’t last forever. Oh, and clean your mouse wheel!” Jiwoo has *yet to* learn every technical word, so later she looked some up with a search engine. Then she texted Daniel: “It’s working now!”
steps.gloss: in charge 담당하는 · crack 금, 갈라진 틈 · mechanism 장치, 구조 · wire 전선 · restore 복구하다 · manufacturer 제조사 · guarantee 보증 · turn down (밝기·소리를) 낮추다 · yet to 아직 ~하지 못한
questions: What was wrong inside the laptop?
What did the technician tell Jiwoo to turn down?

Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What was wrong inside the laptop?" / "What did the technician tell Jiwoo to turn down?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘My ___ keeps ___ing.’로 기기가 자꾸 말썽인 문제를 말할 수 있어요.
‘It stopped working.’과 ‘It won’t turn on.’으로 고장 난 상태를 설명할 수 있어요.

Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 만드는 법 설명하기
steps.goal: 만드는 법을 묻고, 순서대로 설명하고, 주의할 점 말하기
steps.scene_desc: 1월 말 저녁(설 전), 그레이스네 부엌. 가스레인지 위 큰 냄비에서 김이 오르고, 지우가 떡이 담긴 그릇을 들고 손짓으로 순서를 설명하며, 앞치마를 두른 그레이스가 국자를 든 채 웃으며 듣고 있음(글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "How do you make tteokguk?" (만드는 법 설명하기). Goal: 만드는 법을 묻고, 순서대로 설명하고, 주의할 점 말하기. Today's scene: 1월 말 저녁(설 전), 그레이스네 부엌. 가스레인지 위 큰 냄비에서 김이 오르고, 지우가 떡이 담긴 그릇을 들고 손짓으로 순서를 설명하며, 앞치마를 두른 그레이스가 국자를 든 채 웃으며 듣고 있음(글자 없이). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "How do you make ___?".

steps.when: 음식이나 물건을 만드는 법을 물어요. 여기서 you는 ‘(누구든) 사람’.
steps.extra: How do you make tteokguk? · How do you make this sauce?
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "How do you make ___?" (~는 어떻게 만들어요?). When to use it: 음식이나 물건을 만드는 법을 물어요. 여기서 you는 ‘(누구든) 사람’. Note: How do you make tteokguk? · How do you make this sauce?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "First, you need to ___.".

steps.when: 순서대로 설명할 때 첫 단계를 말해요. need to 뒤에는 *동사원형*.

Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.

steps.when: 꼭 지켜야 할 점이나 주의할 점을 말해요. 뒤에 *문장*(you + 동사)이 와요.

Expression 3 of 3: "Make sure you ___." (꼭 ~하세요. ~하는 거 잊지 마세요.). When to use it: 꼭 지켜야 할 점이나 주의할 점을 말해요. 뒤에 문장(you + 동사)이 와요. Note: Make sure you use cold water. · Make sure you don’t stir too much.

steps.title: Tteokguk Lesson · 1월 말, 설을 앞두고 그레이스네 부엌에서

lines.en: Seollal is next week! Jiwoo, {{how do you make}} tteokguk?
lines.ko: 다음 주가 설날이네요! 지우 씨, 떡국은 어떻게 만들어요?

lines.en: It’s easier than it looks. {{First, you need to}} soak the rice cakes in cold water.
lines.ko: 보기보다 쉬워요. 먼저 떡을 찬물에 불려야 해요.

lines.en: Okay, let’s do it step by step. For how long?
lines.ko: 좋아요, 차근차근 해 봐요. 얼마나요?

lines.en: About twenty minutes. Meanwhile, boil some broth in a big pot.
lines.ko: 20분쯤요. 그동안 큰 냄비에 육수를 끓여요.

lines.en: Got it. And then?
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 그다음은요?

lines.en: Next, add the rice cakes. When they float to the top, they’re almost done.
lines.ko: 다음에 떡을 넣어요. 떡이 위로 떠오르면 거의 다 된 거예요.

lines.en: What about the eggs?
lines.ko: 달걀은요?

lines.en: Mix two eggs in a bowl and pour the mixture in slowly. {{Make sure you}} don’t stir too much.
lines.ko: 그릇에 달걀 두 개를 풀어서 천천히 부어요. 너무 많이 젓지 않도록 해요.

lines.en: Why not?
lines.ko: 왜요?

lines.en: Because stirring too much makes the soup cloudy. That’s the secret!
lines.ko: 안 그러면 국물이 탁해지거든요. 그게 비법이에요!

lines.en: And the green onions? Can I use this big knife?
lines.ko: 파는요? 이 큰 칼 써도 돼요?

lines.en: Sure, but it’s really sharp. Let me show you. Then let’s eat together!
lines.ko: 그럼요, 그런데 아주 날카로워요. 제가 보여 줄게요. 그러고 나서 같이 먹어요!

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Tteokguk Lesson · 1월 말, 설을 앞두고 그레이스네 부엌에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Grace: "Seollal is next week! Jiwoo, how do you make tteokguk?" (다음 주가 설날이네요! 지우 씨, 떡국은 어떻게 만들어요?)
2. Jiwoo: "It’s easier than it looks. First, you need to soak the rice cakes in cold water." (보기보다 쉬워요. 먼저 떡을 찬물에 불려야 해요.)
3. Grace: "Okay, let’s do it step by step. For how long?" (좋아요, 차근차근 해 봐요. 얼마나요?)

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: How do you make ___? / And then? / First, you need to ___. Next, add the ___. / Make sure you ___. Table (First, you need to … → Next, …):

steps.title: Grace’s Own Tteokguk
steps.text: On the Saturday before Seollal, Grace followed Jiwoo’s instructions and made tteokguk by herself. The soup *consists of* just a few ingredients: rice cakes, broth, eggs and green onions. Grace measured everything, because the proportion of broth to rice cakes is important. She didn’t have any beef, so she used mushrooms as a substitute. The combination worked perfectly! But she forgot to soak the rice cakes, so she had to start *once more*. “Why did I skip that step *in the first place*?” she laughed. Finally, she combined soy sauce and a little salt, and put thin layers of egg and seaweed on top. Then she *sent out* a photo to her neighbors. Ben replied first: “That looks like proper tteokguk!”
steps.gloss: consist of ~로 이루어지다 · proportion 비율 · substitute 대신 쓰는 것 · combination 조합 · perfectly 완벽하게 · once more 한 번 더 · in the first place 애초에 · layer 층, 겹 · send out (여러 사람에게) 보내다 · proper 제대로 된

steps.scene_desc: 2월 초 평일 점심시간, 회사 근처 작은 공원 벤치. 코트를 입은 지우가 휴대폰을 귀에 대고 통화하며 무릎 위 수첩에 메모하고, 말풍선 없이 작은 원 안에 사무실 책상에서 전화를 받는 마야 팀 동료(조연)가 보임. 그 뒤 유리 회의실 안에 마야(글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Can I leave a message?" (메시지 남기기). Goal: 전화로 사람을 찾고 메시지를 전해 달라고 하기. Today's scene: 2월 초 평일 점심시간, 회사 근처 작은 공원 벤치. 코트를 입은 지우가 휴대폰을 귀에 대고 통화하며 무릎 위 수첩에 메모하고, 말풍선 없이 작은 원 안에 사무실 책상에서 전화를 받는 마야 팀 동료(조연)가 보임. 그 뒤 유리 회의실 안에 마야(글자 없이). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Can I leave a message?".

steps.when: 찾는 사람이 전화를 못 받을 때, *거는 사람*이 써요.

Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "Could you tell her that ___?".

steps.when: 전할 말을 공손하게 부탁해요. tell 뒤에 *사람*, that 뒤에 *전할 문장*.

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Can I leave a message? / Could you tell her that ___? / She’s not available at the moment. / I’ll make sure she gets it. Table (누구에게 → 전할 말 (that …)):
- Could you tell her → that I called?
- Could you tell him → that I’ll be late?
- Could you tell Ms. Park → that I sent the file?
- Could you tell them → that the meeting is at 3?
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
Could you *tell her that* I called? 제가 전화했다고 전해 주시겠어요? 
My coworker *told me that* you called. 동료가 당신이 전화했다고 알려 줬어요. 
tell 바로 뒤에 *사람*(to 없이). that은 빼도 돼요.

Can I *leave* a message? 메시지 남겨도 될까요? — 거는 사람 
Can I *take* a message? 메시지 받아 둘까요? — 받는 사람 
I’ll *get back to* you. 다시 연락할게요.
errors: Could you tell to her that I called?
Could you tell her that I called?
She’s not available on the moment.
She’s not available at the moment.
get back 뒤에 사람이 오면 to.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- tell + 사람 + that + 문장: Could you tell her that I called? 제가 전화했다고 전해 주시겠어요? / My coworker told me that you called. 동료가 당신이 전화했다고 알려 줬어요. / tell 바로 뒤에 사람(to 없이). that은 빼도 돼요.
- leave · take · get back to: Can I leave a message? 메시지 남겨도 될까요? — 거는 사람 / Can I take a message? 메시지 받아 둘까요? — 받는 사람 / I’ll get back to you. 다시 연락할게요.
Common mistakes on screen:
- Could you tell to her that I called? → Could you tell her that I called? (tell 뒤에 사람은 to 없이.)
- Can I leave message? → Can I leave a message? (message 앞에 a.)
- She’s not available on the moment. → She’s not available at the moment. (‘지금은’은 at the moment.)
- I’ll get back you. → I’ll get back to you. (get back 뒤에 사람이 오면 to.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: tell + 사람 + that + 문장: Could you tell her that I called? 제가 전화했다고 전해 주시겠어요? My coworker told me that you called. 동료가 당신이 전화했다고 알려 줬어요. tell 바로 뒤에 사람(to 없이). that은 빼도 돼요.
leave · take · get back to: Can I leave a message? 메시지 남겨도 될까요? — 거는 사람 Can I take a message? 메시지 받아 둘까요? — 받는 사람 I’ll get back to you. 다시 연락할게요.
mistakes: Could you tell to her that I called? → Could you tell her that I called?
Can I leave message? → Can I leave a message?
She’s not available on the moment. → She’s not available at the moment.
I’ll get back you. → I’ll get back to you.

steps.note: 예) her / I called → Can I leave a message? Could you tell her that I called? · 선생님이 전화 받는 사람 역할을 해요.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) her / I called → Can I leave a message? Could you tell her that I called? · 선생님이 전화 받는 사람 역할을 해요. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: her → I called | him → I’ll be late | Maya → I sent the file | Mr. Lee → the meeting is at three.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Can I leave a message?" (메시지 남기기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Can I leave a message?" / "Could you tell her that ___?" / "I’ll get back to you.". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: She’s not available at the moment.
Let me read that back to you.
What’s the best number to reach you?
I’ll make sure she gets it.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 전화 받는 쪽: "She’s not available at the moment." (지금은 통화가 어려우세요., 정중); "Can I take a message?" (메시지를 받아 둘까요?, 정중); "Thanks for calling." (전화 주셔서 감사합니다., 정중)
- 받아 적고 확인하기: "Could you spell your name?" (이름 철자를 말씀해 주시겠어요?, 정중); "Let me read that back to you." (다시 읽어 드릴게요., 정중); "What’s the best number to reach you?" (어느 번호로 연락드리면 될까요?, 정중); "I’ll make sure she gets it." (꼭 전해 드릴게요., 정중)
- 급한 정도 말하기: "It’s urgent." (급한 일이에요., 보통); "There’s no rush." (서두르지 않으셔도 돼요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 전화 낱말

이 과의 전화번호·내선 번호·회사는 수업용 가상 설정이에요.
steps.blank:
A: She’s not ___ at the moment. Can I take a message?   B: Yes. Could you ___ her that I called? 
A: Sure. Could you ___ your name?   B: J-I-W-O-O. It’s not ___, so there’s no rush.

steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 전화 낱말: extension 214 내선 214번 · the main line 대표 번호 / voicemail 음성 사서함 · the operator (대표 전화) 교환원 / a receptionist 접수 담당자 · a customer service representative 고객 상담원 / get down 받아 적다 · call out 큰 소리로 부르다
- 메일·웹 (참고): an attachment 첨부 파일 · a link 링크 · click the link 링크를 누르다 / a website 웹사이트 · a web page 웹 페이지 · log in 로그인하다 / 이 과의 전화번호·내선 번호·회사는 수업용 가상 설정이에요.
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: She’s not ___ at the moment. Can I take a message? B: Yes. Could you ___ her that I called? / A: Sure. Could you ___ your name? B: J-I-W-O-O. It’s not ___, so there’s no rush. / 낱말 상자: available · tell · spell · urgent
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: voicemail (음성 사서함), extension (내선 (번호)), receptionist (접수 담당자), representative (상담원, 담당 직원), appointment (약속, (만날) 예약), mail (우편; 메일), link (링크; 연결), contact (연락처; 연락하다), urgent (급한), rush (서두름; 서두르다), details (자세한 내용), repeat (다시 말하다, 되풀이하다).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

items: What’s the best number to reach you?
They appointed a new team leader.
She’s not available at the moment.
steps.teach:
Word list on screen: reach ((전화로) 연락이 닿다) — "What’s the best number to reach you?"; regarding (~에 관해) — "I’m calling regarding the job."; respond (답하다, 응답하다) — "She’ll respond tonight."; appoint ((자리에) 임명하다) — "They appointed a new team leader."; message (메시지, 전할 말) — "Can I leave a message?"; available ((사람이) 통화·만남이 가능한) — "She’s not available at the moment."; spell (철자를 말하다) — "Could you spell your name?"; return ((전화에) 답하다) — "She’ll return your call."; call (전화; 전화하다) — "Sorry I missed your call."; line (전화(선), 회선) — "Please call the main line.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

steps.role: 번호·전할 말은 *역할 카드*로(이름은 내 이름): 555-0193(가상) · Mr. Han에게 ‘내일 회의를 3시로 옮기고 싶다’ · 급하지 않음.
items: I work with Mr. Han. He’s not available at the moment. (역할 카드)
Sure. Could you spell your name?

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "I work with Mr. Han. He’s not available at the moment. (역할 카드)" (hint on screen: Can I leave a message?)
- "Sure. Could you spell your name?" (hint on screen: ___-___-___. (내 이름 철자))
- "What’s the message?" (hint on screen: Could you tell him that I’d like to move tomorrow’s meeting to three?)
- "What’s the best number to reach you? (번호는 역할 카드)" (hint on screen: It’s 555-0193. There’s no rush.)
Role card on screen (the learner may answer as this role): 번호·전할 말은 역할 카드로(이름은 내 이름): 555-0193(가상) · Mr. Han에게 ‘내일 회의를 3시로 옮기고 싶다’ · 급하지 않음.
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Maya’s Email
steps.text: That evening, Maya got back to Jiwoo via email. It had an attachment and a link to the team’s web page. “Click the link and *log* in to the website to see the job details,” she wrote. “Previously, our team had only two designers, so we really need one more. There’s no immediate rush, but don’t wait too long!” Jiwoo *took off* her coat and read it twice. She *got down* the details in her notebook. She was unable to sit still. “This could *turn into* something big,” she thought. Just then, Grace knocked on her door with some cookies. Jiwoo *called out*, “Come in! I have news!”
steps.gloss: attachment 첨부 파일 · take off (옷을) 벗다 · get down 받아 적다 · unable to ~할 수 없는 · turn into ~이 되다 · call out 큰 소리로 말하다
questions: What was in Maya’s email?
What did Jiwoo get down in her notebook?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Maya’s Email". Text: "That evening, Maya got back to Jiwoo via email. It had an attachment and a link to the team’s web page. “Click the link and log in to the website to see the job details,” she wrote. “Previously, our team had only two designers, so we really need one more. There’s no immediate rush, but don’t wait too long!” Jiwoo took off her coat and read it twice. She got down the details in her notebook. She was unable to sit still. “This could turn into something big,” she thought. Just then, Grace knocked on her door with some cookies. Jiwoo called out, “Come in! I have news!”" Words: attachment 첨부 파일 · take off (옷을) 벗다 · get down 받아 적다 · unable to ~할 수 없는 · turn into ~이 되다 · call out 큰 소리로 말하다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What was in Maya’s email?" / "What did Jiwoo get down in her notebook?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘Can I leave a message?’로 통화가 안 되는 사람에게 메시지를 남길 수 있어요.
‘Could you tell her that ___?’으로 전할 말을 공손하게 부탁할 수 있어요.
‘Let me read that back to you.’로 메시지를 확인하고, ‘I’ll get back to you.’로 답할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘Can I leave a message?’로 통화가 안 되는 사람에게 메시지를 남길 수 있어요.
- ‘Could you tell her that ___?’으로 전할 말을 공손하게 부탁할 수 있어요.
- ‘Let me read that back to you.’로 메시지를 확인하고, ‘I’ll get back to you.’로 답할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 주문이 잘못됐어요
steps.title_en: I’m afraid there’s been a mistake.
steps.goal: 정중하게 실수를 알리고, 무엇이 잘못됐는지 말하고, 해결을 부탁하기
steps.scene_desc: 2월 초 금요일 저녁, 동네 작은 식당 창가 테이블. 지우가 손을 살짝 들어 직원(조연)을 부르며 해산물 파스타 접시를 가리키고, 맞은편의 벤이 미소 지으며 고개를 끄덕임. 창밖은 어두운 겨울 거리(간판·메뉴에 글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "I’m afraid there’s been a mistake." (주문이 잘못됐어요). Goal: 정중하게 실수를 알리고, 무엇이 잘못됐는지 말하고, 해결을 부탁하기. Today's scene: 2월 초 금요일 저녁, 동네 작은 식당 창가 테이블. 지우가 손을 살짝 들어 직원(조연)을 부르며 해산물 파스타 접시를 가리키고, 맞은편의 벤이 미소 지으며 고개를 끄덕임. 창밖은 어두운 겨울 거리(간판·메뉴에 글자 없이). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "I’m afraid there’s been a mistake.".

steps.en: I’m afraid there’s been a mistake.
steps.when: 실수를 정중하게 알릴 때 첫마디로 써요. I’m afraid는 ‘무서워요’가 아니라 ‘미안하지만’.
steps.extra: I’m afraid there’s been a mistake with my order.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "I’m afraid there’s been a mistake." (죄송하지만 착오가 있는 것 같아요.). When to use it: 실수를 정중하게 알릴 때 첫마디로 써요. I’m afraid는 ‘무서워요’가 아니라 ‘미안하지만’. Note: I’m afraid there’s been a mistake with my order.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I ordered ___, but I got ___.".

steps.when: 무엇이 잘못됐는지 분명하게 말해요. 시킨 것도 나온 것도 *과거형*.
steps.extra: I ordered the cream pasta, but I got the seafood pasta.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I ordered ___, but I got ___." (~를 시켰는데 ~가 나왔어요.). When to use it: 무엇이 잘못됐는지 분명하게 말해요. 시킨 것도 나온 것도 과거형. Note: I ordered the cream pasta, but I got the seafood pasta.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Would it be possible to ___?".

steps.when: 아주 공손하게 해결을 부탁해요. to 뒤에 *동사원형*.
steps.extra: Would it be possible to change it? · Would it be possible to get some water?
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Would it be possible to ___?" (~해 주실 수 있을까요?). When to use it: 아주 공손하게 해결을 부탁해요. to 뒤에 동사원형. Note: Would it be possible to change it? · Would it be possible to get some water?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Not My Pasta · 2월 초 금요일 저녁, 동네 식당에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: I’m afraid there’s been a mistake. I ordered ___, but I got ___. / Would it be possible to ___? / Could you check on my order? Table (시킨 것 → 나온 것):
- I ordered the cream pasta, → but I got the seafood pasta.
- I ordered a large coffee, → but I got a small one.
- I ordered hot tea, → but I got iced tea.
- I ordered two salads, → but I only got one.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items: Would it be possible to + 동사원형?

Can you ~?보다 공손해요. 
*Would it be possible to* change it? 바꿔 주실 수 있을까요?
I’m afraid · there’s been · it’s been

*I’m afraid* … 미안하지만 ~(안 좋은 소식을 부드럽게) 
There’s been a mistake. 착오가 있었어요. (’s = *has*) 
*It’s been* forty minutes. 40분이 지났어요.
errors: Would it be possible change it?
Would it be possible to change it?
I’m afraid there’s been a mistakes.
I’m afraid there’s been a mistake.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- Would it be possible to + 동사원형?: Can you ~?보다 공손해요. / Would it be possible to change it? 바꿔 주실 수 있을까요?
- I’m afraid · there’s been · it’s been: I’m afraid … 미안하지만 ~(안 좋은 소식을 부드럽게) / There’s been a mistake. 착오가 있었어요. (’s = has) / It’s been forty minutes. 40분이 지났어요.
Common mistakes on screen:
- Would it be possible change it? → Would it be possible to change it? (possible 뒤에 to + 동사원형.)
- I’m afraid there’s been a mistakes. → I’m afraid there’s been a mistake. (a 뒤에는 하나, mistake.)
- It’s been forty minute. → It’s been forty minutes. (둘 이상이면 minutes.)
- We apologize for the inconvenient. → We apologize for the inconvenience. (for 뒤에는 명사 inconvenience.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) cream pasta / seafood pasta → I ordered cream pasta, but I got seafood pasta. Would it be possible to change it? Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: cream pasta → seafood pasta | a large coffee → a small one | hot tea → iced tea | a chicken salad → a tuna salad.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.teach:
This is the start of session 2 of "I’m afraid there’s been a mistake." (주문이 잘못됐어요); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "I’m afraid there’s been a mistake." / "I ordered ___, but I got ___." / "Would it be possible to ___?". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 문제 말하기: "I think this isn’t what I ordered." (이건 제가 시킨 게 아닌 것 같아요., 정중); "The order is missing something." (주문한 것 중에 뭐가 빠졌어요., 보통); "It’s been forty minutes." (40분이 지났어요., 보통); "Could you check on my order?" (제 주문 좀 확인해 주시겠어요?, 정중)
- 직원이 하는 말: "I’ll sort it out right away." (바로 처리해 드릴게요., 정중); "We apologize for the inconvenience." (불편을 드려 죄송합니다., 정중); "It’s on the house." (무료로 드려요. (가게에서 내는 거예요.), 보통)
- 해결된 뒤: "No harm done." (괜찮아요, 별일 아니에요., 친근); "Thanks for fixing it." (바로잡아 줘서 고마워요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 식당·배달 문제 낱말

*undercooked* 덜 익은 · I was *overcharged*. 돈이 더 청구됐어요. 
a *replacement* 대신 주는 새것 · a *delivery* order 배달 주문

*sort* it out (문제를) 처리하다 · *solve* the problem 문제를 해결하다

공짜로 주는 ‘서비스’는 영어로 It’s *on the house*. 
영어 *service*는 ‘손님 응대’: good *service* 좋은 응대 
*thanks to* ~ ~ 덕분에 · *at this point* 지금으로서는 · *go away* 사라지다

Picture words on screen. New: complaint (불만, 항의), manager (매니저, 책임자), replacement (대신 주는 것, 교체품), delivery (배달), service ((손님) 응대, 서비스), customer (손님, 고객), undercooked (덜 익은), overcharge ((돈을) 더 받다, 과다 청구하다), apologize (사과하다), solve (해결하다, 풀다), insist (고집하다, 꼭 ~하겠다고 하다), inconvenience (불편).

items: I’ll sort it out right away.
Could you check on my order?
steps.teach:
Word list on screen: sort out ((문제를) 처리하다, 해결하다) — "I’ll sort it out right away."; order (주문; 주문하다) — "Could you check on my order?"; mistake (실수, 착오) — "There’s been a mistake."; missing (빠진, 없는) — "The order is missing something."; wrong (잘못된) — "They brought the wrong dish."; check (확인하다) — "Let me check."; late (늦은) — "My food is very late."; on the house ((가게에서) 무료로 주는) — "Dessert is on the house."; harm (해, 피해) — "No harm done.".

What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Have you ever gotten the wrong food at a restaurant? What did you do?
Yes. I said, “I ordered ___, but I got ___.” / No, never.

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Have you ever gotten the wrong food at a restaurant? What did you do?" (hint on screen: Yes. I said, “I ordered ___, but I got ___.” / No, never.)
- "I work at a café. “Here’s your iced latte!” (You ordered a hot latte.)" (hint on screen: I’m afraid there’s been a mistake. I ordered a hot latte, but I got an iced one.)
- "Your food is very late. What do you say?" (hint on screen: It’s been ___ minutes. Could you check on my order?)

steps.title: Ben’s Bad Delivery
steps.text: Over dessert, Ben told Jiwoo about a delivery order last month. His chicken arrived undercooked, and the fries were missing. Besides that, he was overcharged by a considerable amount. He didn’t want to complicate things, so he wrote a short, polite complaint. The manager called him within an hour. “We’re very sorry. *At this point*, we can send a replacement or give you a refund.” Ben chose the replacement, and the manager insisted on returning the extra money, too. *Thanks to* her, Ben’s bad mood quickly *went away*. “Good service doesn’t mean no mistakes,” Ben said. “It means solving them. That night, the manager and I were equally polite. That helped a lot.”

steps.title: 무슨 걱정 있어요?
steps.goal: 걱정을 묻고, 걱정을 말하고, 부드럽게 도움말 주기
steps.scene_desc: 2월 중순 저녁, 그레이스 집 거실의 작은 탁자. 김이 나는 찻잔 두 개, 지우가 두 손으로 찻잔을 감싸고 고민스러운 얼굴로 이야기하고, 그레이스가 메모지와 펜을 내밀며 따뜻하게 웃음. 창가에 화분(글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What’s bothering you?" (무슨 걱정 있어요?). Goal: 걱정을 묻고, 걱정을 말하고, 부드럽게 도움말 주기. Today's scene: 2월 중순 저녁, 그레이스 집 거실의 작은 탁자. 김이 나는 찻잔 두 개, 지우가 두 손으로 찻잔을 감싸고 고민스러운 얼굴로 이야기하고, 그레이스가 메모지와 펜을 내밀며 따뜻하게 웃음. 창가에 화분(글자 없이). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What’s bothering you?".

steps.teach:

Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I’m worried about ___.".

steps.when: 걱정을 털어놓아요. about 뒤에는 명사나 *-ing*.

steps.teach:

Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "It might help to ___.".

steps.title: Tea at Grace’s · 2월 중순 저녁, 그레이스 집에서

lines.en: Here’s your tea. You look a bit down tonight. Is everything okay?
lines.ko: 차 여기요. 오늘 저녁 좀 처져 보여요. 괜찮아요?

lines.en: Not really. It’s about Maya’s team. I thought about it all the way home.
lines.ko: 아니요, 별로요. 마야 팀 일이에요. 집에 오는 내내 그 생각만 했어요.

lines.en: About what? {{What’s bothering you}}?
lines.ko: 무슨 생각이요? 뭐가 마음에 걸려요?

lines.en: {{I’m worried about}} leaving my team. Chloe and I work so well together. And UX design is new for me. What if I can’t do it well?

lines.ko: 목록이라… 좋은 생각이에요. 좋은 점이랑 나쁜 점을 적어 볼게요.

lines.en: Exactly. Try not to worry too much. Whatever you choose, I’m here for you.
lines.ko: 바로 그거예요. 그리고 너무 걱정하지 마요. 뭘 고르든 내가 곁에 있을게요.

lines.en: Thanks, Grace. You know what? I’ll apply. I’ll send my application this week.
lines.ko: 고마워요, 그레이스. 있잖아요, 지원할래요. 이번 주에 지원서를 보낼게요.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Tea at Grace’s · 2월 중순 저녁, 그레이스 집에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Grace: "Here’s your tea. You look a bit down tonight. Is everything okay?" (차 여기요. 오늘 저녁 좀 처져 보여요. 괜찮아요?)
2. Jiwoo: "Not really. It’s about Maya’s team. I thought about it all the way home." (아니요, 별로요. 마야 팀 일이에요. 집에 오는 내내 그 생각만 했어요.)
3. Grace: "About what? What’s bothering you?" (무슨 생각이요? 뭐가 마음에 걸려요?)
4. Jiwoo: "I’m worried about leaving my team. Chloe and I work so well together. And UX design is new for me. What if I can’t do it well?" (지금 팀을 떠나는 게 걱정돼요. 클로이랑 손발이 정말 잘 맞거든요. 그리고 UX 디자인은 처음이에요. 잘 못하면 어쩌죠?)
5. Grace: "I see. So, two worries, your team and the new work. Let’s do it step by step." (그렇군요. 걱정이 두 가지네요, 지금 팀이랑 새 일. 하나씩 차근차근 해 봐요.)
6. Jiwoo: "Okay. It’s been on my mind all week. I don’t know what to do." (네. 일주일 내내 마음에 걸렸어요. 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어요.)
7. Grace: "It might help to make a list. And ask Maya more about the job." (목록을 만들어 보면 도움이 될지도 몰라요. 그리고 마야에게 일에 대해 더 물어봐요.)
8. Jiwoo: "A list… Good idea. I can write down the good and bad points." (목록이라… 좋은 생각이에요. 좋은 점이랑 나쁜 점을 적어 볼게요.)
9. Grace: "Exactly. Try not to worry too much. Whatever you choose, I’m here for you." (바로 그거예요. 그리고 너무 걱정하지 마요. 뭘 고르든 내가 곁에 있을게요.)
10. Jiwoo: "Thanks, Grace. You know what? I’ll apply. I’ll send my application this week." (고마워요, 그레이스. 있잖아요, 지원할래요. 이번 주에 지원서를 보낼게요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

items: Jiwoo is worried about leaving her team.
Grace thinks a list might help.
In the end, Jiwoo decides not to apply.
steps.teach:
True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. Jiwoo is worried about leaving her team.
2. Grace thinks a list might help.
3. In the end, Jiwoo decides not to apply.
The scene they are about:
1. Grace: "Here’s your tea. You look a bit down tonight. Is everything okay?" (차 여기요. 오늘 저녁 좀 처져 보여요. 괜찮아요?)
2. Jiwoo: "Not really. It’s about Maya’s team. I thought about it all the way home." (아니요, 별로요. 마야 팀 일이에요. 집에 오는 내내 그 생각만 했어요.)
3. Grace: "About what? What’s bothering you?" (무슨 생각이요? 뭐가 마음에 걸려요?)
4. Jiwoo: "I’m worried about leaving my team. Chloe and I work so well together. And UX design is new for me. What if I can’t do it well?" (지금 팀을 떠나는 게 걱정돼요. 클로이랑 손발이 정말 잘 맞거든요. 그리고 UX 디자인은 처음이에요. 잘 못하면 어쩌죠?)
5. Grace: "I see. So, two worries, your team and the new work. Let’s do it step by step." (그렇군요. 걱정이 두 가지네요, 지금 팀이랑 새 일. 하나씩 차근차근 해 봐요.)
6. Jiwoo: "Okay. It’s been on my mind all week. I don’t know what to do." (네. 일주일 내내 마음에 걸렸어요. 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어요.)
7. Grace: "It might help to make a list. And ask Maya more about the job." (목록을 만들어 보면 도움이 될지도 몰라요. 그리고 마야에게 일에 대해 더 물어봐요.)
8. Jiwoo: "A list… Good idea. I can write down the good and bad points." (목록이라… 좋은 생각이에요. 좋은 점이랑 나쁜 점을 적어 볼게요.)
9. Grace: "Exactly. Try not to worry too much. Whatever you choose, I’m here for you." (바로 그거예요. 그리고 너무 걱정하지 마요. 뭘 고르든 내가 곁에 있을게요.)
10. Jiwoo: "Thanks, Grace. You know what? I’ll apply. I’ll send my application this week." (고마워요, 그레이스. 있잖아요, 지원할래요. 이번 주에 지원서를 보낼게요.)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: What’s bothering you? / I’m worried about ___.
head: 걱정 (I’m worried about …)
도움말 (It might help to …)
대답
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What’s bothering you? / I’m worried about ___. / It might help to ___. Table (걱정 (I’m worried about …) → 도움말 (It might help to …)):
- my presentation 발표 → …practice it out loud.
- my English test 영어 시험 → …study a little every day.
- the move 이사 → …ask a friend for help.
- my new job 새 일 → …talk to someone on the team.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
I’m *worried about* the interview. 면접이 걱정돼요. 
동사가 오면 -ing: I’m worried about *leaving* my team.

It *might* help to make a list. 목록을 만들면 도움이 될지도 몰라요. 
It *might* snow tonight. 오늘 밤 눈이 올지도 몰라요. 
might 뒤에는 동사원형. 조언이 부드러워져요.
errors: I’m worried about leave my team.
I’m worried about leaving my team.
It might helps to make a list.
It might help to make a list.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- worried about + 명사 · -ing: I’m worried about the interview. 면접이 걱정돼요. / 동사가 오면 -ing: I’m worried about leaving my team.
- might — ~일지도 몰라요: It might help to make a list. 목록을 만들면 도움이 될지도 몰라요. / It might snow tonight. 오늘 밤 눈이 올지도 몰라요. / might 뒤에는 동사원형. 조언이 부드러워져요.
Common mistakes on screen:
- I’m worried about leave my team. → I’m worried about leaving my team. (about 뒤에 동사가 오면 -ing.)
- I’m worry about the interview. → I’m worried about the interview. (‘걱정돼요’라는 기분은 I’m worried.)
- It might helps to make a list. → It might help to make a list. (might 뒤에는 동사원형.)
- What’s bother you? → What’s bothering you? (What’s(= What is) 뒤라서 bothering.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: worried about + 명사 · -ing: I’m worried about the interview. 면접이 걱정돼요. 동사가 오면 -ing: I’m worried about leaving my team.
might — ~일지도 몰라요: It might help to make a list. 목록을 만들면 도움이 될지도 몰라요. It might snow tonight. 오늘 밤 눈이 올지도 몰라요. might 뒤에는 동사원형. 조언이 부드러워져요.
mistakes: I’m worried about leave my team. → I’m worried about leaving my team.
I’m worry about the interview. → I’m worried about the interview.
It might helps to make a list. → It might help to make a list.
What’s bother you? → What’s bothering you?

steps.note: 예) the interview / make a list → A: I’m worried about the interview. B: It might help to make a list.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) the interview / make a list → A: I’m worried about the interview. B: It might help to make a list. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: the interview → make a list | the move → ask a friend for help | my English test → study a little every day | my presentation → practice it out loud.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "What’s bothering you?" (무슨 걱정 있어요?); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "What’s bothering you?" / "I’m worried about ___." / "It might help to ___.". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: Do you want to talk about it?
I can’t stop thinking about it.
I don’t know what to do.
Try not to worry too much.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 걱정을 알아채고 묻기: "You look a bit down." (좀 처져 보여요., 친근); "Is everything okay?" (괜찮아요? 별일 없어요?, 보통); "Do you want to talk about it?" (얘기하고 싶어요?, 보통)
- 걱정 털어놓기: "I can’t stop thinking about it." (자꾸 그 생각이 나요., 보통); "It’s been on my mind." (계속 마음에 걸려요., 보통); "I don’t know what to do." (어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어요., 보통)
- 달래고 힘 주기: "Try not to worry too much." (너무 걱정하지 마요., 보통); "I’m sure it’ll work out." (분명 잘될 거예요., 보통); "I’m here for you." (내가 곁에 있을게요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: worried · anxious · stressed

*worried* 걱정하는 · *anxious* 불안한(더 강함) 
*stressed* 스트레스 받은 — I’ve been so stressed lately. 
명사는 *stress* · *anxiety* · *pressure*: a lot of pressure 큰 부담
vent · cope · reassure

I just need to *vent*. 그냥 털어놓고 싶어요. 
How do you *cope* with stress? 스트레스를 어떻게 견뎌요? 
Grace *reassured* me. 그레이스가 안심시켜 줬어요. 
(참고) 잠 못 드는 날이 오래 이어지면 전문가와 상담해요.
steps.blank:
A: You look a bit ___. What’s bothering you?   B: I’m worried ___ my new job. 
A: It ___ help to make a list. And try not to ___ too much. 
낱말 상자: down · about · might · worry
steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- worried · anxious · stressed: worried 걱정하는 · anxious 불안한(더 강함) / stressed 스트레스 받은 — I’ve been so stressed lately. / 명사는 stress · anxiety · pressure: a lot of pressure 큰 부담
- vent · cope · reassure: I just need to vent. 그냥 털어놓고 싶어요. / How do you cope with stress? 스트레스를 어떻게 견뎌요? / Grace reassured me. 그레이스가 안심시켜 줬어요. / (참고) 잠 못 드는 날이 오래 이어지면 전문가와 상담해요.
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: You look a bit ___. What’s bothering you? B: I’m worried ___ my new job. / A: It ___ help to make a list. And try not to ___ too much. / 낱말 상자: down · about · might · worry
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: stress (스트레스), anxious (불안한, 걱정하는), pressure (압박, 부담), calm (차분한; 진정하다), support (지지(하다), 응원(하다)), insomnia (불면, 잠 못 듦), nightmare (악몽), reassure (안심시키다), vent ((감정을) 털어놓다), upset (속상한), listen (귀 기울여 듣다), worry (걱정하다; 걱정).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

items: My biggest concern is the new work.
How do you cope with stress?
steps.teach:
Word list on screen: bother (신경 쓰이게 하다, 괴롭히다) — "What’s bothering you?"; concern (걱정(거리), 관심사) — "My biggest concern is the new work."; cope (대처하다, 견디다) — "How do you cope with stress?"; anxiety (불안(감)) — "Talking can ease anxiety."; stressed (스트레스 받은) — "I’ve been so stressed lately."; mind (마음, 생각) — "It’s been on my mind."; deal ((deal with) 다루다, 대처하다) — "I can deal with it."; situation (상황) — "It’s a hard situation."; advice (조언) — "Thanks for the advice.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Imagine a friend looks a bit down. What do you say?
You look a bit down. What’s bothering you?
What do you worry about before a big change?
Your friend is worried about a presentation. Give some advice.
How do you calm down when you feel stressed?
I usually ___. / Taking a walk helps me.
Ask me what’s on my mind.
Is everything okay? What’s bothering you?
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Imagine a friend looks a bit down. What do you say?" (hint on screen: You look a bit down. What’s bothering you?)
- "What do you worry about before a big change?" (hint on screen: I’m often worried about ___.)
- "Your friend is worried about a presentation. Give some advice." (hint on screen: It might help to ___.)
- "How do you calm down when you feel stressed?" (hint on screen: I usually ___. / Taking a walk helps me.)
- "Ask me what’s on my mind." (hint on screen: Is everything okay? What’s bothering you?)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
questions: Imagine a friend looks a bit down. What do you say?
What do you worry about before a big change?
Your friend is worried about a presentation. Give some advice.
How do you calm down when you feel stressed?

steps.title: Jiwoo’s List
steps.text: Back in her apartment, Jiwoo took Grace’s advice seriously and made a list. On the left, she wrote her worries: leaving Chloe and her team, and learning UX design. On the right: new skills, bigger projects, and app design. The list didn’t take *that much* time, but it helped a lot. Somehow, the constant noise in her head got quieter. Outside, the sky was threatening snow, but Jiwoo felt calm. She sent Maya two questions. “Everyone is *bound to* feel nervous,” Maya answered. Before midnight, Jiwoo opened the application form.
steps.gloss: seriously 진지하게 · that much 그렇게 많이 · somehow 어쩐지, 왠지 · constant 끊임없는 · threaten (나쁜 날씨 등이) 올 것 같다 · bound to 틀림없이 ~하다
questions: What did Jiwoo write on the left side?
What did Jiwoo open before midnight?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Jiwoo’s List". Text: "Back in her apartment, Jiwoo took Grace’s advice seriously and made a list. On the left, she wrote her worries: leaving Chloe and her team, and learning UX design. On the right: new skills, bigger projects, and app design. The list didn’t take that much time, but it helped a lot. Somehow, the constant noise in her head got quieter. Outside, the sky was threatening snow, but Jiwoo felt calm. She sent Maya two questions. “Everyone is bound to feel nervous,” Maya answered. Before midnight, Jiwoo opened the application form." Words: seriously 진지하게 · that much 그렇게 많이 · somehow 어쩐지, 왠지 · constant 끊임없는 · threaten (나쁜 날씨 등이) 올 것 같다 · bound to 틀림없이 ~하다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What did Jiwoo write on the left side?" / "What did Jiwoo open before midnight?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘What’s bothering you?’로 걱정이 있는지 부드럽게 물을 수 있어요.
‘I’m worried about ___.’로 걱정을 말할 수 있어요.
‘It might help to ___.’로 부드럽게 도움말을 줄 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘What’s bothering you?’로 걱정이 있는지 부드럽게 물을 수 있어요.
- ‘I’m worried about ___.’로 걱정을 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘It might help to ___.’로 부드럽게 도움말을 줄 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

lessons.title: 어떤 사람이에요?
lessons.goal: 어떤 사람인지 묻고, 성격을 문장으로 묘사하고, 사이를 말하기

steps.title: 어떤 사람이에요?
steps.goal: 어떤 사람인지 묻고, 성격을 문장으로 묘사하고, 사이를 말하기
steps.scene_desc: 2월 말 오후, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 대니얼이 노트를 펼쳐 둔 채 커피잔을 들고 묻고, 지우가 손짓하며 누군가를 설명하듯 웃으며 이야기함. 창밖은 겨울 끝 햇살(글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What’s she like?" (어떤 사람이에요?). Goal: 어떤 사람인지 묻고, 성격을 문장으로 묘사하고, 사이를 말하기. Today's scene: 2월 말 오후, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 대니얼이 노트를 펼쳐 둔 채 커피잔을 들고 묻고, 지우가 손짓하며 누군가를 설명하듯 웃으며 이야기함. 창밖은 겨울 끝 햇살(글자 없이). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What’s ___ like?".

steps.when: 성격·분위기를 물어요. 생김새를 묻는 What does ___ look like?와 달라요.
steps.extra: What’s your team leader like?
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "What’s ___ like?" (~는 어떤 사람이에요?). When to use it: 성격·분위기를 물어요. 생김새를 묻는 What does ___ look like?와 달라요. Note: What’s your team leader like?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "He’s the kind of person who ___.".

steps.en: He’s the kind of person who ___.
steps.when: 성격을 한 문장으로 그려요. 여기서 *who*가 주어라서, 동사를 그 사람에 맞춰요.
steps.extra: She’s the kind of person who plans everything in advance.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "He’s the kind of person who ___." (그는 ~하는 사람이에요.). When to use it: 성격을 한 문장으로 그려요. 여기서 who가 주어라서, 동사를 그 사람에 맞춰요. Note: She’s the kind of person who plans everything in advance.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "We get along well.".

steps.when: 둘 사이를 말해요. get along (with) = 잘 지내다.
steps.extra: Chloe and I get along well.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "We get along well." (우리는 사이가 좋아요.). When to use it: 둘 사이를 말해요. get along (with) = 잘 지내다. Note: Chloe and I get along well.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("What’s She Like? · 2월 말 오후, 동네 카페에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

frame: He’s the kind of person who ___. / We get along well.
