steps.teach:
Word list on screen: simpler (더 단순한(simple의 비교급)) — "Life was simpler."; war (전쟁(여기서는 놀이 water war 물싸움)) — "a water war with the kids next door"; ordinary (평범한) — "It was an ordinary summer day."; era (시대) — "the cassette era"; remember (기억하다) — "Do you remember that summer?"; vacation (방학, 휴가) — "summer vacation"; together (함께) — "We played together every day."; days ((those days) 그 시절) — "I miss those days."; back ((back then) 그때(에)) — "Things were different back then.".

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What would you do every summer as a kid?" (hint on screen: We would ___ every summer.)
- "What was different back then?" (hint on screen: Back then, we didn’t ___. / Life was simpler.)
- "What did you spend hours doing as a teenager?" (hint on screen: I spent hours ___ing.)
- "Do you ever feel nostalgic? When?" (hint on screen: Yes, when I ___. / Not really. I like now better.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.

steps.title: The Great Water War
steps.text: That night, Ben told Jiwoo about one ordinary summer from his youth. When he was ten, the kids on his street would have a huge water battle every August. They called it “the Great Water War.” Ben’s little army had six soldiers, and their only weapons were water guns and water bombs. The enemy was the kids from the next street. “We would get completely wet, and then everyone would eat ice cream together,” Ben said. As teenagers, those friends *went through* a lot together, and they still write to each other. Before going inside, Jiwoo shared her own news. This fall, her new team will start working with a team overseas. A new chapter is about to begin.
steps.gloss: ordinary 평범한 · youth 어린(젊은) 시절 · battle 싸움 · army 군대(여기서는 ‘우리 편’) · soldier 군인(여기서는 ‘편 아이’) · weapon 무기 · enemy 상대편 · go through (힘든 일을) 겪다 · overseas 해외의 · chapter (인생의) 한 장

What is Jiwoo’s news?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "The Great Water War". Text: "That night, Ben told Jiwoo about one ordinary summer from his youth. When he was ten, the kids on his street would have a huge water battle every August. They called it “the Great Water War.” Ben’s little army had six soldiers, and their only weapons were water guns and water bombs. The enemy was the kids from the next street. “We would get completely wet, and then everyone would eat ice cream together,” Ben said. As teenagers, those friends went through a lot together, and they still write to each other. Before going inside, Jiwoo shared her own news. This fall, her new team will start working with a team overseas. A new chapter is about to begin." Words: ordinary 평범한 · youth 어린(젊은) 시절 · battle 싸움 · army 군대(여기서는 ‘우리 편’) · soldier 군인(여기서는 ‘편 아이’) · weapon 무기 · enemy 상대편 · go through (힘든 일을) 겪다 · overseas 해외의 · chapter (인생의) 한 장.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What did the kids on Ben’s street do every August?" / "What is Jiwoo’s news?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘We would ___ every summer.’로 예전에 되풀이해서 하던 일을 말할 수 있어요.
‘Things were different back then.’과 ‘Back in the day, ___.’로 옛날 모습을 말할 수 있어요.
‘I miss those days.’와 ‘Time flies.’로 그 시절을 그리워하는 마음을 말할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘We would ___ every summer.’로 예전에 되풀이해서 하던 일을 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘Things were different back then.’과 ‘Back in the day, ___.’로 옛날 모습을 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘I miss those days.’와 ‘Time flies.’로 그 시절을 그리워하는 마음을 말할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.
